All 20 test suites pass, including the previously failing character range formatting cases.

The fix in `include/fmt/ranges.h`:
- Added `is_string_format` / `is_debug` flags and a `write_debug_string` helper to `range_formatter` (include/fmt/ranges.h:391-411)
- Rewrote `range_formatter::parse` to accept C++23 `s` and `?s` specifiers for character ranges: `s` sets `"` brackets with no separator and disables per-element debug formatting; `?s` marks a debug string; both error unless the element type is `Char` (include/fmt/ranges.h:437-460)
- `format` short-circuits the `?s` case to write the whole range as an escaped, quoted debug string (include/fmt/ranges.h:474-478)

Results: `fmt::format("{:s}", vector<char>{'a','\n','\t'})` → `"a\n\t"` (with literal newline/tab), `"{:?s}"` → `"a\n\t"` (escaped), and `{::s}` works for nested char ranges.
